### porousPlate3d

The porous plate problem is implemented as described in [@guo2002coupled] and [@peng2003simplified].
To test the coupled model's accuracy and to determine its EOC, a numerical simulation of the porous plate problem including a temperature gradient and natural convection in a square cavity is used.
The porous plate problem describes a channel flow, where the upper cool plate moves with a constant velocity, and through the bottom warm plate a constant normal flow is injected and withdrawn at the same rate from the upper plate.
At the left and right hand sides of the domain a periodic boundary condition is applied and constant velocity and temperature boundary conditions are applied to the top and bottom plates according to @fig-porousplateprob-3d.

![Schematic representation of the porous plate's simulation setup including the boundary conditions.](/examples/thermal/porousPlate2d/doc/fig/porousPlateSetup.png){#fig-porousplateprob-3d width="60%"}

An analytical solution for the given steady-state problem is provided for the velocity and temperature distributions by

$$
\begin{aligned}
 u_x(y) & =u_{x,0}\left(\frac{e^{Re \cdot y/L}-1}{e^{Re}-1}\right) , \\
T(y) & =T_0+ \Delta T\left(\frac{e^{Pr \cdot Re \cdot y/L} -1}{e^{Pr \cdot Re}-1}\right) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-porousPlateAnalytical-3d}

Here $u_{x,0}$ is the upper plate's velocity, $Re = \frac{u_{y,0} L}{\nu}$ the Reynolds number depending on the injected velocity $u_{y,0}$, the fluid's viscosity $\nu$, and the channel length $L$.
The temperature difference between the hot and cold plate is given by $\Delta T=T_h-T_c$.
First, a couple of simulations are implemented to scale the velocity and temperature profiles for a range of the Reynolds number and Prandtl number.
The relative global error is computed via [@guo2002coupled]

$$
E= \frac{\sqrt{\sum \limits_{i} |T(x_i)-T_a(x_i)|^2}}{\sqrt{\sum \limits_{i} |T_a(x_i)|^2}} \quad ,
$$

where the summation is over the entire system and $T_a$ is the analytical solution @eq-porousPlateAnalytical-3d.
The `porousPlate3dSolver` variant implements the same simulation, but additionally illustrates the application of the solver class concept.
